Criminal Case Dossier: The Locked Homestead & The Snakebite Claim
Jurisdiction: Maharashtra, India
Primary Allegations / Charges: Murder (Section 302 IPC) and Cruelty by Husband/Relatives (Section 498A IPC)
Type of Evidence: Purely circumstantial, medical forensics, and conduct-based inferences
1. Key Individuals & Their Roles
Person	Identity / Role	Relevant Context
Revata (Victim)	Deceased; married to the primary accused for ~2 years	Lived in the marital home in a rural village.
Trimukh (Accused No. 1)	Husband of the deceased	Resided under the same roof; present in the house on the night of the incident.
In-laws (Accused Nos. 2–4)	Parents and brother of Trimukh	Resided in the same joint household / compound.

4. Forensic & Medical Findings
The body was dispatched for a formal post-mortem examination. The medical report revealed the following:
Snakebite Analysis: No puncture marks, fang impressions, localized tissue necrosis, or signs of hemotoxic/neurotoxic snake venom were found anywhere on the body.
External Injuries: Prominent, horizontal contusions and ligature-like abrasions were observed around the front and sides of the neck. Multiple small fingernail abrasions and contusions were present near the chin and collarbone.
Internal Injuries: Fracture of the hyoid bone (neck bone) with extensive extravasation of blood into the subcutaneous neck tissues.
Official Cause of Death: Asphyxia due to manual strangulation / violent throttling.

Official Cause of Death: Asphyxia due to manual strangulation / violent throttling.
Time Since Death: Consistent with the late hours of the night when all occupants were inside the home.
5. Physical Scene & Conduct Evidence
Exclusive Possession: The incident occurred inside a closed residential room where the husband and wife were the sole occupants during the night. No sign of a break-in, forced entry, or external trespass was found.
Absence of Immediate Alarm: No shout, cry for help, or distress call was raised by the accused during the night to alert immediate neighbors.
Absence of Medical Intervention: Despite a primary health center being located 3 km away, the accused did not take her to a qualified medical doctor, claiming they preferred a traditional healer located 15 km away.

Behavior Following Death: When the police arrived to seize the body, Trimukh and his family were unable to produce the healer they claimed to have visited and subsequently fled the village, remaining untraceable for nearly two weeks before being apprehended.
6. Key Analytical Dimensions to Weigh
The "Last Seen" / Exclusive Knowledge Principle: In Indian criminal jurisprudence (specifically Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act), when an act takes place inside the privacy of a home where outsiders have no access, how far does the burden shift onto the inmates of the house to explain how the death occurred?

Plausibility of Defense: Does offering an objectively false explanation (snakebite vs. clear strangulation) serve merely as a weak defense, or does it become an active, incriminating link in the chain of circumstantial evidence?
Individual vs. Shared Liability: Given that multiple family members lived in the house, does the evidence prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the husband personally executed the act, or could it have been an individual act of another family member without his direct participation?
